props.gloss_en: the mishna's first clause: the keva of a gentile['s animal] and of a neveila is forbidden
the mishna's last clause: a tereifa that suckled from a kosher [animal] -- its keva is permitted
Rav Chisda: the first clause -- [it is forbidden because] it looks like eating neveilot
Rav Chisda: here [the tereifa] there is slaughter
R' Yochanan: here -- before the retraction
R' Yochanan: here -- after the retraction
R' Yochanan: and a mishna does not move from its place
R' Yochanan: one may curdle with the keva of neveilot
R' Yochanan (per R' Chiyya bar Abba): one may not curdle with the keva of a gentile's slaughter
R' Shimon bar Abba: in accordance with whom? with R' Eliezer
R' Eliezer: a gentile's unspecified intent is for idolatry
R' Yochanan (per Rav Shmuel bar Rav Yitzchak): one may curdle both with the keva of a neveila and with the keva of a gentile's slaughter
without concern for the words of R' Eliezer
one may not curdle with the skin of a neveila's stomach
and [one may curdle] with the keva of a kosher [animal] that suckled from a tereifa
and all the more so with the keva of a tereifa that suckled from a kosher [animal]
what is the reason? the milk collected in it is mere secretion
